title: The Multi-State Cooperative Societies Rules, 2002
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture, Department of Agriculture and Cooperation
source_citation: The Multi-State Cooperative Societies Rules, 2002, G.S.R. 790(E), 2 December 2002
content: The Multi-State Cooperative Societies Rules, 2002 were made under section 124 of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002. The Rules call themselves the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Rules, 2002 and state that they come into force on publication in the Official Gazette. They define terms used for administration under the Act, including Act, authorised office, decree, defaulter, form and general meeting. For a case-specific question, consult the applicable Rule and current official text.

title: Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023
source_citation: Ministry of Cooperation, official booklet current as on 19 December 2024
content: The Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2023 amends the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002. The Ministry of Cooperation describes its purpose as incorporating provisions of the 97th Constitutional Amendment and strengthening governance, transparency, accountability and the election process in multi-state cooperative societies. The Ministry's official booklet states that the Act came into force on 3 August 2023. Legal answers must be grounded in the relevant current provision rather than treating this overview as a substitute for the Act.

title: Model Bye-laws for Primary Agricultural Credit Societies: Official Overview
source_citation: Ministry of Cooperation Annual Report 2023-24, Model Bye-laws for PACS
content: The Ministry of Cooperation states that Model Bye-laws are intended to let PACS diversify into more than 25 business activities. The official overview lists examples including dairy, fishery, floriculture, godowns, food-grain procurement, fertilizer and seed distribution, short-term and long-term credit, custom hiring centres, fair price shops, community irrigation, Business Correspondent activities and Common Service Centre services. The overview also says the model bye-laws aim to make PACS membership more inclusive and broad-based, with representation for women and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. State adoption and the applicable registered bye-laws must be checked before relying on a particular activity or membership rule.

title: Guidelines on Computerization of PACS Project
source_citation: Ministry of Cooperation, Guidelines on Computerization of PACS Project
content: The Ministry of Cooperation describes PACS computerization as a Centrally Sponsored Project approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on 29 June 2022. The official guidelines describe computerization of about 63,000 functional PACS over five years, with a total outlay of Rs. 2,516 crore. They describe a national ERP-based software to digitize PACS services and link PACS with District Central Cooperative Banks and State Cooperative Banks. The official project page lists three assistance components: hardware, National Level PACS Software or ERP, and a System Integrator. It says the project is intended to improve service delivery, transparency, efficiency, loan processing, audit and accounting.
